amendments.rule: In a construct chain, the English relational expression belongs to the nomen rectum, headed on that noun. This is normally *of*, handled exactly as a Greek genitive `of + noun`, but where the ASV recasts the construct relation with *from*, *for*, *in*, *to*, *over*, or another preposition, that expression belongs there too. The construct state of the first noun is what signals the relation, but the first noun's unit takes only its own English word. **The rectum may be a pronominal suffix rather than a noun, and nothing changes.** Where the ASV renders such a suffix not with a possessive but with *of* and a pronoun — `כֻּלָּם` → *all of them*, `מַרְבִּיתָם` → *the greatest part of them* — the whole *of + pronoun* is the suffix's one unit, headed on the pronoun under rule 24, and the construct noun keeps only its own word: `כֹּל` takes *all*, never *all of*. Do not read that *of* as part of an English quantifier or as licensed by the construct noun's own state, for the reason this rule's third sentence gives. The corpus aligns a suffix to *of them* headed on *them* in 116 units and records no `כֹּל` → *all of* treatment, and where the construct noun's own English is something else the division shows in a single unit: `כֻּלָּם` → *five of them in all* gives *in all* to `כֹּל` and *of them* to the suffix. Where the ASV writes a possessive or a bare pronoun instead, rule 18 governs as before and there is no *of* to place.
amendments.why: Rule 19's wording assumed a noun rectum, so it did not say where the *of* goes when the rectum is a pronominal suffix. EZK.32 read that silence the wrong way in six verses, giving `כֹּל` *all of* and leaving the suffix bare *them*, against rule 19's own third sentence. The amendment closes the gap where the over-broad silence stands rather than adding a cross-referencing rule elsewhere. Evidence: rule 19's third sentence; the corpus's 116 `הוּא` units aligned to *of them* headed on *them*; the absence of any `כֹּל` → *all of* treatment at count 3 or more among 2105 `כֹּל` units in 301 chapters; and 1CH.2.6, where `כֻּלָּם` → *five of them in all* gives `כֹּל` only *in all* and so shows the division directly. The last sentence keeps rule 18's ordinary possessive case untouched.

conventions: `כֹּל` with a pronominal suffix: the construct takes only *all* and the suffix takes the whole *of them*, headed on the pronoun. The suffix fills the rectum slot, so rule 19 places the *of* there and leaves the construct noun its own word. Where the ASV writes no *of* at all, as in 32.12's *are they all*, the suffix takes only the pronoun. Applied at 32.12, 32.22, 32.23, 32.24, 32.25, 32.26 and 32.30.

`שָׁמָּה` (D + Sd) at 32.29 and 32.30 is rendered by a bare *There*, which is `שָׁם`'s own word and not a fusion carrying the directive: the adverb takes it and the Sd is `unrepresented` under rule 32's last sentence. This matches the plain `שָׁם` -> *There is* / *is there* at 32.22, 32.24 and 32.26, so the whole `שָׁם` series reads alike. Rule 32's `שָׁמָּה` -> *thither* fusion is the other branch and the ASV does not take it here. BSB represents both Sd tokens; that is the documented convention difference, not an error.

In the repeated `סְבִיבוֹת` grave formula, read whether `הָיָה` is written before applying rule 49. At 32.22, 32.25 and 32.26 no verb stands and the preposition carries the supplied *are round about* under rule 49; at 32.23 and 32.27 a written `הָיָה` takes the copula itself and `סָבִיב` keeps only *round about*. At 32.24 the ASV writes no copula at all, so there is nothing to place.

The 1cs suffix of `אֲדֹנָי` is `unrepresented` throughout (32.3, 32.8, 32.11, 32.14, 32.16, 32.31, 32.32): the ASV writes *the Lord*, with the supplied *the* going to the title under rule 15 and no *my* anywhere for the suffix to take. These are seven of the chapter's BSB disagreements and none is a correction candidate.

report: Checked all 52 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end for added-word asymmetries the table cannot see, since it is keyed by source lemma and blind to `added` units.

Real error, six verses: the construct `כֻּלָּם` rendered *all of them* gave the partitive *of* to `כֹּל`. Rule 19 gives the relational expression to the rectum and says the first noun's unit takes only its own English word; the rectum here is the pronominal suffix. The corpus agrees: `הוּא` suffixes align to *of them* headed on *them* in 116 units; no `כֹּל` -> *all of* treatment appears at count 3 or more among 2105 `כֹּל` units; and 1CH.2.6 `כֻּלָּם` -> *five of them in all* gives `כֹּל` only *in all*, leaving *of them* to the suffix. Patched EZK.32.22, 32.23, 32.24, 32.25, 32.26 and 32.30: `כֹּל` now takes *all* alone and the suffix takes *of them*, headed on the pronoun.

EZK.32.12 is deliberately unpatched: the ASV writes *are they all* with no *of* to place, so `כֹּל` keeps *all* and the suffix keeps *they* under rules 18 and 40. After the patch the chapter reads `כֹּל` one way everywhere, never taking more than its own word.

Candidates checked and left alone because the source licenses the difference: `עַל־פְּנֵי` fuses to *before* in 32.10 but splits into *upon* and *open* in 32.4, which is rule 30's one-English-word subtraction test; `סָבִיב` carries the supplied copula under rule 49 in 32.22, 32.25 and 32.26 but not in 32.23 or 32.27, where a written `הָיָה` takes it; the waw is rendered *And*, *also*, *Yea*, *then*, *But* and *yet* as the ASV writes it; the article is aligned or unrepresented as the ASV writes a *the* or not; `חַלְלֵי־חֶרֶב` is bare or takes the supplied *them that are* as the ASV writes it; and `שָׁם` differs only in ASV word order, heading on *there* in all five occurrences.

The four `added` *even*s (32.6, 32.21, 32.31, 32.32) beside the one aligned *even* (32.18) are consistent rather than a split: rule 16 gives the word only to a marker standing on the very phrase it introduces, and only 32.18's `אוֹתָהּ` does. Likewise 32.27's italic *they* is `added` while 32.25 `נִתָּן` -> *he is put* and 32.30 `בּוֹשִׁים` -> *they are put to shame* keep their supplied pronouns, because a verbless clause has no morpheme to carry a referential subject pronoun and a written participle does.

BSB: no genuine error among the 21 disagreements. The seven `אֲדֹנָי` suffixes are the documented convention difference (the ASV writes *the Lord*, not *my Lord*); the rest are morphemes the ASV leaves unrendered under rules 22, 27, 32 and 40 (resumptive suffixes in 32.7, 32.8 and 32.9; the paragogic nun in 32.6 and the paragogic he twice in 32.19; the `לֵ` of `לֵאמֹר` in 32.17; the dative `לְ` recast as a bare indirect object in 32.25; the articles on `הַנֹּפְלִים` in 32.22 and 32.24, for which the ASV writes neither a *the* nor a relative). Nothing here was changed to move the rate.

EZK.32.30's suffix on `חִתִּיתָם` keeps the whole expansion *which they caused* under rule 18, but the competing reading (mark *which ... caused* `added` under rule 20's lexical-verb boundary, giving the suffix only *they*) is now named in that unit's note, which rule 8 wanted and the verse pass had omitted. EZK.32.16's *wherewith* on the object suffix, with the opening waw left `unrepresented`, already named its competing reading and is unchanged.
EZK.32.11's *upon* on the verb rather than the suffix is consistent with 32.2's `נִדְמֵיתָ` -> *Thou wast likened unto*, so the earlier correction recorded in that verse holds across the chapter.
